title: Invoice Review and Actions — Fusion ERP
summary: Review supplier invoices and prepare or execute explicitly confirmed creation, line cancellation or whole-invoice cancellation. Shows exact targets and proposed values, then verifies outcomes through invoice and line reads. Unpublished draft; validate destination permissions and runtime support.

platform.product: Oracle AI Database Private Agent Factory

connectionContext: Existing Fusion invoice read and action sources; endpoint and credentials remain environment-local.

memory.description: No persistent memories or cross-thread context.

capabilities: Invoice reads, creation, cancellation and line cancellation through separate read/action REST sources.
Exact-target proposals, explicit confirmation, no automatic retry of ambiguous writes, and independent invoice/line readback before reporting success.
prerequisites: PAF 26.7-compatible visual Agent Builder and a registered model.
Confirmed Fusion demo endpoint and a suitably scoped integration account.
Factory POST cancellation support described in integrations/fusion-apps/runtime/README.md; valid accounting period and distribution combinations for creation.

tools.name: Get invoice lines
tools.purpose: Verify created item lines, target-line cancellation and other returned line effects.

tools.name: Cancel line
tools.purpose: Cancel the specifically confirmed invoice line.

safetyControls: Write-capable unpublished draft. A new USD 0.02 fixture was created, one line canceled, then the whole invoice canceled and independently verified; destination validation is still required.
Conversational confirmation is an instruction, not a server-enforced approval mechanism. Restrict integration-account permissions and add an external approval gateway before unattended use.
Do not retry an ambiguous write automatically. Do not claim payment, posting or approval capabilities.
setup: Import the release .paf into an unpublished destination flow.

Import assets/invoice-read-openapi.json and assets/invoice-actions-openapi.json as separate REST sources. Replace the example server URL with your confirmed Fusion endpoint and configure authentication in PAF. These reconstructed contracts require target-release validation.

Select AIW26-PAF-HOL6004-BOO6096 on every Agent node. This OpenAI Compatible connection is configured on the prepared PAF instance and is the required model for the final AI World lab instances. Configure that same model name in each destination; model definitions and credentials are not bundled.
Create or select the sources listed in assets/source-bindings.json; replace every environment-local node binding.

Verify the exact POST cancellation guard support in integrations/fusion-apps/runtime/README.md before testing actions. Use valid accounting dates, item lines and distribution combinations; inspect action media-type headers.
Check permissions and connectivity against the intended demo environment before publishing.

Read the numbered sticky notes from left to right. Agent Description provides workflow details and sample questions; use its expand control to read the full guide. The 2026-10-18 layout/model update preserves the workflow wiring and documented memory mode; the earlier validation record describes the original demo runs.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: List up to five supplier invoices and explain which fields need review. Do not change anything.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: Prepare the exact proposal for an invoice change I specify. Show the target and required fields; do not execute it.

expectedOutcomes: Evidence is distinguished from assumptions and unavailable data.
Writes require a specific user-confirmed proposal; drafts are not reported as executed.

validation.environment: the prepared PAF instance; the editor account; authorized Fusion HTTPS endpoint
validation.status: Create, line cancellation and whole-invoice cancellation independently verified; fixture canceled
notes: The editor-owned Build draft uses AIW26-PAF-HOL6004-BOO6096. Publication and memory settings were preserved. Both REST nodes now use separately authenticated, editor-owned read/action sources with a verified private payables account.

Read/action contracts now include explicit Content-Type parameters. Creation includes item lines and distribution combinations; exact invoice and child-line reads support reconciliation. Agent Description explains the left-to-right workflow, action proposals, confirmation, verification and two sample questions.

A unique USD 0.02 test invoice with two USD 0.01 item lines was proposed without writing. An independent exact-number GET found no invoice before and after the proposal. After explicit confirmation, separate Fusion reads verified one matching invoice and both item lines.

A line-cancellation proposal made no write. The first confirmation was blocked by Factory before reaching Fusion because its POST intent check did not recognize cancellation. The reviewed runtime patch was applied to Build only, with backup, restart and readiness checks. A renewed explicit confirmation then canceled the selected item line; an independent GET verified its amount was zero and the other item line remained USD 0.01.

Fusion also returned two zero-value tax lines, and the header stayed USD 0.02 while the item-line sum became USD 0.01. The agent disclosed that discrepancy without issuing a corrective write. Line cancellation does not by itself establish an updated header amount.

A whole-invoice cancellation proposal made no write. After explicit confirmation, independent Fusion GETs verified CanceledFlag=true, header amount USD 0.00 and all returned lines at zero with DiscardedFlag=true. The fixture is canceled; no pre-existing invoice was used as a write target.

All three supported action outcomes were established by separate reads. Raw Factory tool traces were not captured, so exact tool-call counts are not independently asserted. Conversational confirmation remains an instruction, while the integration account enforces destination permissions; no grants were changed.

After the changes, Chromium found no node overlaps, card-width mismatches or clipped sticky notes. The official encrypted export matched the live graph; only local REST bindings were cleared in the portable workflow. Final-instance deployment has not started.
